title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
data_curation: Data comes from an agent-driven 'AutoResearch-style' flywheel. Strong foundation models build a per-domain function tree (knowledge coverage) and a capability profile, and compile them into a task-synthesis skill. Agents then synthesize tasks, environment states and state-based verifiers. A step-level VLM judge mines SFT data from both successful and failed trajectories: maximal contiguous correct steps, the first step of each reflection/exploration phase, and recovery segments. The paper finds this matches or beats keeping only verifier-passed full trajectories. For online RL, coding agents distill data-injection skills, build coherent cross-app user states, have an LLM generate tasks filtered by an LLM judge, and write code verifiers validated by multi-model rollouts plus a VLM judge, yielding about 10,000 task-verifier pairs. Environments cover redroid-containerized MobileWorld, OSWorld VMs with bash, Playwright web and Serper/Jina DeepSearch (up to 10,000 parallel sandboxes), plus 100+ real phones running 150+ apps. Failure-analysis agents route model errors into new targeted tasks.
curriculum: Training has three stages, SFT → Action RL → Online RL, wrapped in the flywheel. Bootstrapping uses multiple rounds of rejection sampling (following MAI-UI) to build an initial SFT corpus. Each later iteration evaluates the model, diagnoses failures, synthesizes targeted tasks and retrains. In SFT, one expert per domain (mobile, desktop, web, DeepSearch) is trained mainly on its own domain plus a controlled cross-domain mix, and the experts are then merged into one checkpoint. A small share of verified-correct, self-sampled general/math/code/tool data is mixed in to preserve general ability; questions the starting model already solves work better than ones it fails. Online RL uses a model-adaptive curriculum: an active pool holds tasks with intermediate success rates, unsolved tasks sit in a low-budget monitoring pool until they start succeeding, and mastered tasks are monitored and reactivated if performance drops.
method: This is a native multimodal GUI agent at 27B (primary), 35B-A3B and 4B. Its unified action space combines GUI actions (click, long_press, drag, type, open, system_button…), cli_command (bash, or ADB shell on Android), api_call, ask_user and terminate. It can emit batched action sequences in one turn. SFT uses sliding windows of 5 steps with stride 4: earlier screenshots are dropped but text history is kept, and the overlap step is loss-masked. Action RL targets six recurring error patterns (confusable grounding, sorting/ranking, quantity completeness, premature completion, loops, long-tail actions) using mined and actively explored data. Its per-step reward is r = F·(w_type·C + w_arg·C·Q − λ_sens·S − λ_rep·L), with entropy regularization and reasoning-length bounds to prevent collapse. Online RL is a tailored GRPO with binary terminal verifier rewards over trajectories of 100+ turns, run on about 10,000 concurrent environments, with virtual displays giving roughly 20x real-phone rollout throughput. A harness adds notification-driven proactive service (event → affair → task with memory) and an OpenClaw-like cross-device planner.
eval_metrics: Mobile: MobileWorld GUI-only (117 tasks, SR), the new MobileWorld-Real (409 human-written tasks over 104 apps on live phones, scored by AutoJudge: 5-VLM majority vote over pass/failed/env_error, 92.8% agreement with experts on 666 trajectories), and AndroidDaily. Computer: OSWorld-Verified and OSWorld-v2 (partial/binary, steps/task). Web: WebArena (with corrected references and scripts), BrowseComp/-ZH. Grounding: ScreenSpot-Pro/V2, MMBench-GUI L2, OSWorld-G-Refined, UI-Vision. General/agentic: MMMU-Pro, MMLU-Pro, IFEval, Tau2, Terminal-Bench 2.0, Claw-Eval, BFCL-v4, SkillsBench. Headlines for the 27B model: MobileWorld 82.1 (85.5 at 100 steps), MobileWorld-Real 92.2, AndroidDaily 97.5, OSWorld-Verified 79.5 (2nd to Opus 4.8's 83.4), OSWorld-v2 40.0/13.9, WebArena 73.6, ScreenSpot-Pro 81.5 with zoom.
key_results: The 27B model sets mobile SOTA: 82.1% on MobileWorld (vs Seed 2.1 Pro 73.2, Opus 4.8 67.5) and 92.2% on MobileWorld-Real (vs Seed 2.1 Pro 88.7). It reaches 73.6% on WebArena (vs Opus 4.8 71.9) and 79.5% on OSWorld-Verified, while lifting Terminal-Bench 2.0 to 50.1 vs 41.1 for the Qwen3.5-27B base comparison. Action RL raises task SR by more than 7% while cutting reasoning tokens 21.3%. Online RL increases trajectories containing a verification action by 14.7% and cuts false stops by 11.2%.
evolution_note: This report continues MAI-UI (step-level trajectory judge, GRPO-style online RL, rejection-sampled SFT) and joins the 2026 wave of native GUI agents (UI-TARS-2, GUI-Owl-1.5, UI-Venus-1.5, EvoCUA) that scale verifiable environments and online RL. It pushes past sandbox benchmarks: a 100+-phone real-device runtime and the MobileWorld-Real benchmark target the sim-to-real gap it documents in Qwen3.7-Plus failures. Its hybrid GUI+CLI batched action space, where online RL produces a 'Bash as hands, GUI as eyes' pattern, and its agent-driven data flywheel point toward agents that partly build their own training curricula.
